title: Valuation of a field norm over a finite semilocal DVR algebra
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$. Let $B$ be a commutative integral domain containing $A$ which is finite as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and let $L=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ be a finite extension of $K$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-vector-space-dimension] through this inclusion. Suppose that the set $X$ of maximal ideals of $B$ is finite, that every $\mathfrak q\in X$ contracts to the maximal ideal of $A$, that each $B_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a discrete valuation ring, and that $f_{\mathfrak q}=[B/\mathfrak q:k]$ is finite. For any discrete valuation ring $R$ with fraction field $F$, write $v_R:F^\times\to\mathbf Z$ for its normalized valuation: $v_R(x)=r$ when $x=u t^r$ for a unit $u\in R^\times$ and a uniformizer $t$ of $R$, with $r\in\mathbf Z$. Define $N_{L/K}(y)$ to be the determinant [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant] over $K$ of the $K$-linear map $L\to L$, $z\mapsto yz$. Then for every $y\in L^\times$ one has $$v_A(N_{L/K}(y))=\sum_{\mathfrak q\in X}f_{\mathfrak q}\,v_{B_{\mathfrak q}}(y).$$

source.place: Tag 02MJ (lemma-finite-extension-dim-1), norm/order formula specialized to discrete valuation rings, with order expressed as normalized uniformizer exponent.

proof.text: Embed B into L and take its A-linear image M. The fraction-ring map is injective, so M is A-linearly isomorphic to B and is finite over A [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Its K-span is L [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]: apply Mathlib IsFractionRing.ideal_span_singleton_map_subset with a = 1 and b = Set.univ, using algebraicity from Module.Finite A B. This is the algebraic clearing-of-denominators argument for the lattice B in Tag 02MJ.

First fix nonzero b in B and let g be multiplication by b on L. Its image N = bM lies in M. Apply [lem-exc-dvr-lattice-distance-determinant] to M and g: the negative quotient N/(M intersect N) is zero. The positive quotient M/N is A-linearly isomorphic to B/bB via B isomorphic to M, using Submodule.Quotient.restrictScalarsEquiv and Submodule.Quotient.equiv. Thus B/bB has finite A-length and its length equals v_A(det_K(g)) = v_A(Norm(b)) [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant, def-weil-pbc-module-length].

Finite A-length implies both the ascending and descending chain conditions, hence finite B-length, since a chain of B-submodules is a chain of A-submodules. Apply [lem-exc-semilocal-restriction-length] to B/bB. Identify its canonical residue fields with A/(q under A) and B/q through Ideal.quotEquivOfEq and Ideal.bijective_algebraMap_quotient_residueField. The induced ring maps commute by Ideal.ResidueField.map_algebraMap, so Algebra.finrank_eq_of_equiv_equiv identifies the residue degrees; a semilinear surjection transports their finiteness.

For each maximal q, put R = B_q [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The localization of B/bB [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is R/(b/1)R: Submodule.localized'_span identifies the localized principal ideal, and IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv applied to Submodule.toLocalizedQuotient' gives the quotient isomorphism. Its R-length is Ring.ord R (b/1) by definition. This order is finite since b/1 is nonzero and R is a Noetherian DVR [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Ring.ordFrac_eq_ord and Ring.ordMonoidWithZeroHom_eq_coe identify its natural-valued length with WithZero.log (Ring.ordFrac R (b in FractionRing B)). Converting the finite length sum from ENat to integers proves the asserted formula for every nonzero b in B.

Use IsFractionRing.div_surjective to write y = a/b with a and b nonzero. The norm is multiplicative, so the logarithmic order of Norm(y) plus that of Norm(b) equals that of Norm(a); all norms are nonzero because they are images of units. In each B_q the same equality follows from multiplicativity of Ring.ordFrac and WithZero.log_mul, using that IsLocalization.algEquiv commutes with the maps from B. Subtract the integral formulas for a and b and distribute the finite sum and residue-degree factors. This proves the desired identity for every unit y, including negative local valuations.

Step 1: the K-span of B is a finite-dimensional domain inside L, so it is a field equal to L. Step 2: the lattice node is applied with M=B and g=multiplication by y; the sign agrees with 02MI/02MG, where d(M,gM)=l(M/H)-l(gM/H). Step 3: finite A-length gives finite B-length, the 02M0 node is applied to both quotients, and they are subtracted in Z. Step 4: localization embeds in L, H_q=R∩yR by the common denominator st, the localized quotient maps are surjective, and Frac(B_q)=L. Step 5: the ideals over (t^n) give length n, and the cases r≥0 and r<0 are both written out. Step 6: substitution.
